reader.requirement: At 1985, when an OPEN of a sequential file succeeds, the record delimiter in force is the one the RECORD DELIMITER clause of that file-name's own file control entry specifies (the default method when it has none), whatever another entry naming the same physical file specifies.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.Cite picks the edition's citation text in the COBOL7598/COBOL7599 messages only; the check and the method are edition-independent

reader.edition-search: grep RecordDelimiter over src (non-generated): no ConstructRegistry construct, no VersionConformancePass visitor, no DialectBehavior; SequentialConnector consults DialectBehavior only for LINAGE; the DialectLevel passed by EmitFileRegistration does not reach framing
reader.witnesses-cover: part: witnesses cover the clause per file; not two entries naming one physical file with different delimiters

probes.printed: FB (BINARY-SEQUENTIAL) writes and reads FB1 00 04, FB2 00 05; FL (LINE-SEQUENTIAL) on the same physical file writes and reads FL1 00 04, FL2 00 05; FB then opens the line-written file: FBOPEN 39, READ after the failed OPEN FB3 47
probes.expected: each OPEN uses its own entry's delimiter; the binary entry does not adopt the line method of the medium (OPEN refused 39, then READ 47 on the unopened file)

probes.printed: FB, FL, FN opened together each use their own method (bytes as in 1985-GR-VII.2.8.4-3)

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.2.8.4 GR5  (║2.8.4 General Rules║)  the text is in GR5

reader.notes: The delimiter is bound per file control entry at compile time and registered with that file's connector, so every OPEN of that file-name uses it. The status 39 on a medium written by the other method is an implementor detection, not something this rule requires.

refuter.evidence: Probe refute-1985-238/rdelz.cob (runs/rdelz-001) at --std 85: after FN (no clause) wrote the binary-framed medium, FL (RECORD DELIMITER IS LINE-SEQUENTIAL, same ASSIGN) OPEN EXTEND 00 and WRITE 00 appended 'XYZ' CR LF (od of RDELZ.DAT): at the successful OPEN the delimiter in force is FL's own entry's, not the medium's. The reader's rdel2 shows the other direction refused at OPEN (39), which VII.4.3.4 GR8 leaves to the implementor; GR5 binds only a successful OPEN. Mixed media from EXTEND are a consequence of the program, not a GR5 breach. cite.py: OK  §1985:VII.2.8.4 GR5 the text is in GR5.
